title: EKSU ACC 316 - Advanced International Financial Reporting Standards (AIFRS) | Practice Bank

questions.stem: Under IFRS 5, what is the primary criterion for classifying an asset or disposal group as held for sale?

options.A: The asset must be actively marketed.
options.B: The sale is expected to be completed within five years.
options.C: Management has committed to a plan to sell the asset, and the sale is highly probable.
options.D: The asset's carrying amount is higher than its fair value less costs to sell.

questions.stem: When an asset or disposal group is classified as held for sale under IFRS 5, how should it be measured?

options.A: At its original cost less accumulated depreciation.
options.B: At the lower of its carrying amount and its fair value less costs to sell.
options.C: At its fair value less costs to sell, regardless of its carrying amount.
options.D: At its estimated future selling price.

questions.stem: What is the minimum presentation requirement for assets held for sale in the statement of financial position under IFRS 5?

options.A: They must be presented as part of property, plant, and equipment.
options.B: They must be presented separately as current assets.
options.C: They must be presented separately as non-current assets, but not as current assets.
options.D: They must be presented separately on a dedicated line item within assets.

questions.stem: Under IFRS 5, which of the following conditions must be met for an operation to be classified as discontinued?

options.A: The operation has been sold during the reporting period.
options.B: The operation represents a separate major line of business or geographical area of operations, and is part of a single coordinated plan to dispose of it.
options.C: The operation has ceased to generate revenue.
options.D: The operation's losses exceed its revenues in the current period.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a minimum disclosure requirement on the face of the statement of comprehensive income for discontinued operations under IFRS 5?

options.A: The net profit or loss from discontinued operations.
options.B: The total revenue of the discontinued operation.
options.C: The total expenses of the discontinued operation.
options.D: The fair value of the assets of the discontinued operation.

questions.stem: Which IFRS standard addresses the accounting for exploration and evaluation of mineral resources?

options.A: IFRS 4
options.B: IFRS 6
options.C: IFRS 8
options.D: IFRS 11

questions.stem: Under IFRS 6, what are the elements of the cost of an exploration and evaluation asset?

options.A: Only directly attributable external costs.
options.B: All costs incurred up to the point where commercial extraction can begin.
options.C: Costs that can be directly attributed to the exploration and evaluation of specific mineral resources.
options.D: Only the costs of acquiring exploration and evaluation licenses.

questions.stem: What does the term "Exploration and evaluation assets" refer to under IFRS 6?

options.A: Assets that are held for sale after exploration activities.
options.B: Expenditures that have been capitalized as exploration and evaluation assets.
options.C: Assets that have been fully developed and are ready for production.
options.D: Intangible assets related to mineral rights.

questions.stem: According to IFRS 6, "Exploration and evaluation expenditure" refers to:

options.A: All costs incurred by an entity in connection with the exploration for and evaluation of mineral resources before the determination of the commercial viability of extracting a mineral resource.
options.B: Only the costs of drilling and seismic surveys.
options.C: Expenditures related to the sale of mineral resources.
options.D: Costs incurred after the commencement of commercial production.

questions.stem: "Exploration for and evaluation of mineral resources" under IFRS 6 encompasses:

options.A: The discovery of mineral deposits.
options.B: The assessment of the technical feasibility and commercial viability of extracting a mineral resource.
options.C: The sale of extracted mineral resources.
options.D: The decommissioning of mining facilities.

questions.stem: In segment reporting, which of the following is a primary test for identifying reportable segments based on revenue?

options.A: The segment's profit margin compared to the consolidated profit.
options.B: The segment's revenue (external and internal) is 10% or more of the total revenue.
options.C: The segment's assets are 10% or more of the consolidated assets.
options.D: The segment's operating expenses are 10% or more of the consolidated expenses.

questions.stem: If a segment's external revenue is N50 million and its internal revenue is N150 million, and the total consolidated revenue is N280 million (after eliminations), what is the total revenue for this segment?

options.A: N50 million
options.B: N150 million
options.C: N200 million
options.D: N280 million

questions.stem: According to the provided data, if the total external revenue of LUCIDITY limited is N295 million, which segment would qualify as reportable if the revenue test is 10% of total external revenue?

options.A: Electronics (N50 million)
options.B: Restaurants (N20 million)
options.C: Recreational clubs (N40 million)
options.D: Travel agencies (N75 million)

questions.stem: In the context of LUCIDITY limited's segments, if "Reconciling items and elimination" amount to N150 million in total, this represents:

options.A: Inter-segment revenues and eliminations.
options.B: External revenues not yet recognized.
options.C: Profits from the sale of assets.
options.D: Unallocated corporate expenses.

questions.stem: Which of the following revenue figures for a segment would *not* qualify as a reportable segment if the threshold is 10% of N280 million (consolidated revenue)?

options.A: N30 million
options.B: N28 million
options.C: N20 million
options.D: N40 million

questions.stem: IFRS 11 identifies two types of joint arrangements. What are they?

options.A: Joint Ventures and Jointly Controlled Assets
options.B: Joint Operations and Joint Ventures
options.C: Jointly Controlled Entities and Joint Operations
options.D: Jointly Controlled Operations and Jointly Controlled Entities

questions.stem: In a joint operation under IFRS 11, a joint operator recognizes:

options.A: Its share of the assets and liabilities of the joint operation.
options.B: Only its share of the revenue generated by the joint operation.
options.C: Its share of the net profit or loss of the joint operation.
options.D: Its share of the capital contributions made to the joint operation.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a characteristic of a joint arrangement under IFRS 11?

options.A: One party has control over the arrangement.
options.B: The arrangement involves two or more parties.
options.C: The arrangement is established for a single transaction.
options.D: The arrangement is a wholly-owned subsidiary.

questions.stem: When a joint operator recognizes its share of the assets and liabilities in a joint operation, it is essentially accounting for:

options.A: The entire joint operation as a separate entity.
options.B: Its individual assets, liabilities, revenues, and expenses related to the joint operation.
options.C: Only the assets contributed by the joint operator.
options.D: The capital invested by all joint operators.

questions.stem: What is the primary distinction between a joint operation and a joint venture under IFRS 11?

options.A: Joint operations involve shared assets and liabilities, while joint ventures involve equity accounting.
options.B: Joint ventures involve shared assets and liabilities, while joint operations involve equity accounting.
options.C: Joint operations are always unincorporated, while joint ventures are always incorporated.
options.D: Joint ventures have separate legal status, while joint operations do not.

questions.stem: According to IFRS 11, a joint operator recognizes its share of the following elements in relation to joint operations:

options.A: The revenues and expenses incurred by the other joint operator.
options.B: Its assets contributed to the joint operation.
options.C: Its share of the assets it controls jointly.
options.D: Its share of the total liabilities of the joint operation, regardless of its control.

questions.stem: IFRS 13 establishes a framework for measuring fair value. What is the fundamental principle of fair value measurement under IFRS 13?

options.A: The price an entity would receive to sell an asset or pay to transfer a liability in an orderly transaction between market participants at the measurement date.
options.B: The historical cost of the asset or liability.
options.C: The price an entity would receive to sell an asset at a discount.
options.D: The price based on management's best estimate of value.

questions.stem: IFRS 13 defines fair value as:

options.A: The amount an asset was acquired for.
options.B: The amount an entity would need to pay to replace an asset.
options.C: The exit price received to sell an asset or paid to transfer a liability.
options.D: The intrinsic value of an asset.

questions.stem: According to IFRS 13, what does the term "market participants" refer to in the context of fair value measurement?

options.A: Participants in the entity's own market.
options.B: Buyers and sellers in the principal market for the asset or liability.
options.C: Only professional investors.
options.D: Customers who are willing to pay any price.

questions.stem: An "orderly transaction" in the context of IFRS 13 fair value measurement means:

options.A: A transaction at the end of the reporting period.
options.B: A transaction that is not a forced liquidation or distressed sale.
options.C: A transaction that involves only cash.
options.D: A transaction with a related party.

questions.stem: IFRS 13 categorizes fair value measurements into a three-level hierarchy based on:

options.A: The size of the entity.
options.B: The type of asset or liability.
options.C: The observability of inputs to valuation techniques.
options.D: The length of time the asset has been held.

questions.stem: Which level of the fair value hierarchy under IFRS 13 includes inputs that are not based on observable market data?

options.A: Level 1
options.B: Level 2
options.C: Level 3
options.D: All levels include non-observable data.

questions.stem: Level 1 inputs in the IFRS 13 fair value hierarchy are:

options.A: Unobservable inputs derived from internal models.
options.B: Observable inputs that are quoted prices in active markets for identical assets or liabilities.
options.C: Observable inputs other than quoted prices in active markets for identical items.
options.D: Inputs that are significant but not directly observable.

questions.stem: Level 2 inputs in the IFRS 13 fair value hierarchy are:

options.A: Quoted prices in active markets for identical assets or liabilities.
options.B: Observable inputs other than quoted prices in active markets for identical items, such as quoted prices for similar assets or liabilities in active markets.
options.C: Unobservable inputs derived from internal data.
options.D: Inputs that require significant management judgment.

questions.stem: What is the main objective of IFRS 13?

options.A: To introduce new requirements for when fair value accounting is required.
options.B: To establish a single framework for measuring fair value and enhance disclosures related to it.
options.C: To mandate the use of fair value for all assets and liabilities.
options.D: To eliminate the use of historical cost accounting.

questions.stem: Under IFRS 5, a disposal group is a group of assets to be disposed of together as a group in a single transaction, and liabilities directly associated with those assets that will be transferred in the transaction. What is a key condition for classifying it as held for sale?

options.A: The group must be actively advertised for sale.
options.B: The disposal must be expected to be completed within one year of the classification date.
options.C: Management must have committed to a plan to sell the group.
options.D: The liabilities must exceed the assets in the group.

questions.stem: How are assets classified as held for sale presented in the statement of financial position under IFRS 5?

options.A: Within their existing categories, but with a disclosure.
options.B: Separately from other assets, as current assets if sale is within one year.
options.C: Separately on a line item as "Assets Held for Sale".
options.D: As a deduction from equity.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a criterion for classifying an operation as discontinued under IFRS 5?

options.A: It represents a separate major line of business or geographical area of operations.
options.B: It is part of a single coordinated plan to dispose of a separate major line of business or geographical area of operations.
options.C: It is an operation that has ceased to exist entirely.
options.D: It is a disposal of a subsidiary or other group of assets that form a disposal group.

questions.stem: What is the minimum disclosure required on the face of the statement of comprehensive income for discontinued operations?

options.A: Details of assets and liabilities.
options.B: A single amount representing the net profit or loss from the discontinued operation.
options.C: Detailed breakdown of revenues and expenses.
options.D: Information about the buyer.

questions.stem: IFRS 6 provides guidance on the accounting for exploration and evaluation expenditures. Which of the following is considered a cost element under this standard?

options.A: General administrative overheads not directly related to a specific project.
options.B: Depreciation of plant and equipment used in exploration.
options.C: Costs of acquiring exploration rights.
options.D: Research and development costs for new extraction technologies.

questions.stem: Which of the following definitions best fits "Exploration and evaluation assets" under IFRS 6?

options.A: Assets acquired for future development.
options.B: Expenditures recognized in accordance with IFRS 6 in the accounting for the exploration for and evaluation of mineral resources.
options.C: Assets used in the sale of mineral resources.
options.D: Intangible assets representing mineral reserves.

questions.stem: The process of "Exploration for and evaluation of mineral resources" under IFRS 6 involves:

options.A: Only the drilling of exploratory wells.
options.B: Activities undertaken to discover a potential for commercially viable mineral resources, and then assessing the technical and commercial feasibility of extracting them.
options.C: The extraction and sale of mineral resources.
options.D: The transportation of extracted minerals.

questions.stem: In segment reporting, if a segment's revenue is N25 million and the total consolidated revenue is N300 million, would it be considered a reportable segment based on the revenue test (10% threshold)?

options.A: Yes, because N25 million is greater than N30 million.
options.B: No, because N25 million is less than N30 million.
options.C: Yes, because N25 million is a significant portion of N300 million.
options.D: No, because the segment must be profitable to be reportable.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of "Reconciling items and elimination" in segment reporting?

options.A: To increase the reported revenue of segments.
options.B: To eliminate inter-segment transactions and ensure that consolidated revenues reflect external sales.
options.C: To add back expenses not allocated to segments.
options.D: To show the profit of each segment individually.

questions.stem: Under IFRS 11, a "joint arrangement" requires:

options.A: Control by a single party.
options.B: A contractually agreed sharing of control over the economic activities of the arrangement.
options.C: The establishment of a separate legal entity.
options.D: A unanimous decision-making process for all operational matters.

questions.stem: When a joint operator accounts for its share of assets and liabilities in a joint operation, it recognizes:

options.A: The fair value of all assets in the joint operation.
options.B: Its share of assets and liabilities it controls jointly.
options.C: Only the assets it has contributed.
options.D: The entire liabilities of the joint operation.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of a joint arrangement under IFRS 11?

options.A: Two or more parties have an agreement.
options.B: The parties share control over the arrangement.
options.C: One party has sole control over the arrangement.
options.D: The arrangement involves significant economic activity.

questions.stem: In a joint venture, a joint operator typically accounts for its investment using:

options.A: The fair value method.
options.B: The equity method.
options.C: The cost method.
options.D: The consolidation method.

questions.stem: Under IFRS 13, the "principal market" for an asset or liability is:

options.A: The market with the highest price.
options.B: The market where the entity normally transacts.
options.C: The market that maximizes the volume of transactions for the asset or liability.
options.D: The market with the greatest liquidity.

questions.stem: Which level of the fair value hierarchy is most reliant on unobservable inputs and management judgment?

options.A: Level 1
options.B: Level 2
options.C: Level 3
options.D: None of the above, all levels are equally reliable.

questions.stem: When an asset or disposal group is classified as held for sale under IFRS 5, it is measured at the lower of its carrying amount and:

options.A: Its original cost.
options.B: Its fair value.
options.C: Its fair value less costs to sell.
options.D: Its recoverable amount.

questions.stem: Under IFRS 5, what is the primary condition that signifies an operation is discontinued?

options.A: It has incurred a net loss for the period.
options.B: It is a separate major line of business or geographical area of operations that is disposed of or held for sale.
options.C: It is no longer part of the entity's primary business activities.
options.D: Its results are presented separately in the financial statements.

questions.stem: In the context of IFRS 6, "Exploration and evaluation assets" are recognized when:

options.A: Commercial discovery of mineral resources is confirmed.
options.B: The entity has rights to explore in a specific area and intends to carry out exploration and evaluation.
options.C: Production of minerals has commenced.
options.D: Feasibility studies are completed.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT an example of an exploration and evaluation expenditure that could be capitalized under IFRS 6?

options.A: Geological and geophysical surveys.
options.B: Expenditure for drilling exploratory wells.
options.C: Administrative overheads allocated to exploration activities.
options.D: Costs of evaluating the technical feasibility and commercial viability of an ore body.

questions.stem: If a segment's external revenue is N15 million and its internal revenue is N5 million, and the total consolidated revenue is N280 million, what is the total revenue for this segment?

options.A: N15 million
options.B: N20 million
options.C: N25 million
options.D: N280 million

questions.stem: According to IFRS 11, a joint arrangement is characterized by:

options.A: The absence of a contractual agreement.
options.B: Shared control by two or more parties.
options.C: Sole control by one party.
options.D: The operation of a fully owned subsidiary.

questions.stem: In a joint operation, a joint operator recognizes its share of:

options.A: The revenues earned by the entire joint operation.
options.B: The assets and liabilities it controls jointly.
options.C: The profit or loss before considering its share.
options.D: The capital contributed by all parties.

questions.stem: Which level of the fair value hierarchy uses quoted prices in active markets for identical assets or liabilities?

options.A: Level 1
options.B: Level 2
options.C: Level 3
options.D: Not applicable to IFRS 13.

questions.stem: Under IFRS 5, how are assets held for sale presented in the statement of financial position?

options.A: They are grouped with similar assets but labelled as held for sale.
options.B: They are presented separately as a current asset if the sale is expected within one year.
options.C: They are presented separately on a line item as 'Assets Held for Sale', with no depreciation charged.
options.D: They are reclassified as intangible assets.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes a "discontinued operation" under IFRS 5?

options.A: An operation that has stopped generating profits.
options.B: An operation that is being sold, is already sold, or is closed down, and represents a separate major line of business or geographical area.
options.C: An operation that is undergoing restructuring.
options.D: An operation whose management has been changed.

questions.stem: Under IFRS 6, "Exploration and evaluation expenditure" includes:

options.A: Costs incurred after commercial viability has been established.
options.B: Expenditures incurred before the determination of the commercial viability of extracting a mineral resource.
options.C: Costs of plant and equipment used in the extraction phase.
options.D: Expenses related to the sale of mineral resources.

questions.stem: Which of the following would NOT be considered a reportable segment based on the revenue test (10% of total consolidated revenue of N280 million), if the segment's external revenue is N25 million and internal revenue is N3 million?

options.A: Segment Revenue: N28 million
options.B: Segment Revenue: N20 million
options.C: Segment Revenue: N30 million
options.D: Segment Revenue: N25 million

questions.stem: IFRS 11 distinguishes between joint operations and joint ventures. A joint venture is characterized by:

options.A: Joint control over assets and liabilities.
options.B: The right to the assets and obligations for the liabilities of the arrangement.
options.C: The establishment of a separate entity where parties have an interest and account for it using the equity method.
options.D: Direct recognition of revenues and expenses.

questions.stem: Under IFRS 13, Level 3 fair value measurements are characterized by:

options.A: Direct observation of market prices for identical items.
options.B: Use of observable inputs for similar items.
options.C: Reliance on unobservable inputs that are significant to the measurement.
options.D: Application of the entity's own assumptions without market validation.
